newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices steady in slow market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices steady in slow market.

text.p: Millfeed prices were mostly steady on Tuesday but with a negative bias amid featureless activity, dealers said.
Dealers cited bearish factors such as livestock feeding on pasture which diminished millfeeds demand, buyers turning to cheaper ingredients and ample supplies weighing on the nearby positions.
"Other feed ingredients are going down, like hominy and gluten feed, and the CBOT corn futures are dropping," one North Carolina broker said. "It's got the buyers backing away from the market."
For the Carolinas, spot offers dropped $3 a short ton to $90.00 a ton.
Feed business was relatively slow due to seasonal concerns, a Chattanooga dealer said.
"But I would not agree that buyers were going to substitute against midds," he said. "I think midds are a relatively decent buy."
